+  ok=JE_Initiate

+//! JEScript native piece/work attributes for a single punch, per Quintin Smits's MIT Agie Processor.
+use super::AgieJob;
+
+fn attribute(lines: &mut Vec<String>, object: &str, context: &str, key: &str, value: &str) {
+    lines.push(format!(
+        "  ok=JE_AttribObject({object},SETATTR,je_piece,{context},{key},{value},je_dim)"
+    ));
+}
+
+fn quoted(value: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
+    format!("\"{value}\"")
+}
+
+pub(super) fn piece(job: &AgieJob, name: &str, separation_length_mm: f64) -> String {
+    let [x, y, z] = job.stock_min;
+    let [right, back, top] = job.stock_max;
+    let height = format!("{:.3}", top - z);
+    let group = quoted(name);
+    let work = format!("{group},\"CUT1\"");
+    let work_context = format!("{work},NULL");
+    let start_context = format!("{work},\"stp1\"");
+    let mut lines = vec!["'$Include \"jescript.sbh\"".into(), "sub SetOrigin".into()];
+    for (field, value) in [
+        ("ID_HEIGHT", height.clone()),
+        ("ID_NOMEOBJ", name.into()),
+        ("ID_MATERIAL", "0001".into()),
+        ("ID_THREAD", "Berco Cut 0.25".into()),
+        ("ID_POSX", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_POSY", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_POSZ", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_ROTATION", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_DIML", format!("{:.3}", right - x)),
+        ("ID_DIMB", format!("{:.3}", back - y)),
+        ("ID_POSPOSX", format!("{x:.3}")),
+        ("ID_POSPOSY", format!("{y:.3}")),
+        ("ID_POSPOSZ", format!("{z:.3}")),
+        ("ID_VALSECP", "3.0".into()),
+        ("ID_VALRETP", "30.0".into()),
+    ] {
+        attribute(&mut lines, "PIECE", "NULL,NULL,NULL", field, &quoted(value));
+    }
+    lines.extend([
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecauto,c_tecauto_t)".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecassign,c_tecass_fi)".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecalert,c_tecalert_sea)".into(),
+        "end sub".into(),
+        "sub CutPunch".into(),
+        format!("  ok=JE_Create(GROUP,je_piece,{group},NULL)"),
+        format!("  ok=JE_Create(WORK,je_piece,{work})"),
+    ]);
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "WORK",
+        &work_context,
+        "ID_GEOMETRY",
+        &quoted(format!("AGIE.USING_{name}.ISO")),
+    );
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_PUNCH", "c_punch");
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_WORKCOND", "\"2\"");
+    // The control selects its own offsets and passes for the expressly selected Fine Ra0.30
+    // technology. No controller technology tables or previously programmed parts are embedded.
+    lines.push("  ok=JE_CreateQuality(je_piece,\"QN2\",\"0.30,1.50,1.00,F,F,F\",je_q1)".into());
+    for (field, value) in [
+        ("ID_QUALITY", "je_q1".into()),
+        ("ID_THREAD", quoted("Berco Cut 0.25")),
+        ("ID_ENTRYMODE", "c_entper".into()),
+        ("ID_HEIGHT", quoted(&height)),
+        ("ID_POSX", quoted("0")),
+        ("ID_POSY", quoted("0")),
+        ("ID_SEPCUT", quoted(format!("{separation_length_mm:.1}"))),
+        ("ID_REVCUT", quoted("T")),
+        ("ID_COMMPOINTENTRY", quoted("3.0")),
+        ("ID_COMMPOINTEXIT", quoted("0")),
+        ("ID_PRIORITY", quoted("10")),
+        ("ID_RADIUSMINLA", quoted("T")),
+        ("ID_I_TYPE", "c_radius_rm".into()),
+        ("ID_E_TYPE", "c_radius_rm".into()),
+        ("ID_ENTRY", quoted("2")),
+    ] {
+        attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, field, &value);
+    }
+    lines.push(format!(
+        "  ok=JE_CreateStartPoint(WORK,\"stp1\",je_piece,{work})"
+    ));
+    for (field, value) in [("ID_POSX", job.start[0]), ("ID_POSY", job.start[1])] {
+        attribute(
+            &mut lines,
+            "STARTPOINT",
+            &start_context,
+            field,
+            &quoted(format!("{value:.3}")),
+        );
+    }
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_STP", "\"stp1\"");
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_STPMODE", "c_work");
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "STARTPOINT",
+        &start_context,
+        "ID_STP_PL",
+        "\"4\"",
+    );
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "STARTPOINT",
+        &start_context,
+        "ID_DIAMETER",
+        "\"2.0\"",
+    );
+    lines.extend([
+        format!("  ok=JE_GenerateCuts(WORK,je_piece,{work},ASDELETE,NULL)"),
+        format!("  ok=JE_GenerateCuts(WORK,je_piece,{work},ASAGIE,NULL)"),
+        "end sub".into(),
+        "sub main".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_Initiate".into(),
+        "  if (ok=0) then".into(),
+        "    SetOrigin".into(),
+        "    CutPunch".into(),
+        "    ok=JE_AttribObject(PIECE,SETATTR,je_piece,je_grp,NULL,NULL,ID_STATEGY,\"EW\",je_dim)"
+            .into(),
+        "    ok=JE_ClosePiece(je_piece)".into(),
+        "  else".into(),
+        "    stop".into(),
+        "  end if".into(),
+        "end sub".into(),
+        String::new(),
+    ]);
+    lines.join("\r\n")
+}

+## #2945 - Native Agie wire job for a rectangular punch
+
+Write the ISO geometry, SBR reference and SBL job in CamCraft. Use the existing post crate for the writer. Keep document checks and nominal geometry extraction in the app. The post crate uses tempfile for same-volume staging and rustix or windows-sys for an atomic rename that cannot replace another job. These dependencies already occur in the lockfile. No new dependency between CamCraft crates is needed. An external generator would add an installation requirement.
+
+Use the Classic 2S template from #2946. The operator adds the AGIE_QN2 condition and selects the 1 mm separation length. The template stays unconfigured until then. Use nominal geometry because the resident control determines the wire offsets and trims. Applying the preview gap to the exported contour would compensate twice.
+
+Limit the first job to one captured rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. The offline control plotted the 0.25 mm Berco wire outside the punch. Its rough centre offset was 0.245 mm. Adding the 0.125 mm wire radius and rounding outward gives a 0.4 mm stock margin. The entry needs 3 mm of straight face on either side. The control cuts the separate 1 mm interval after the long passes. Other thicknesses, conditions, profiles and separation lengths need separate control evidence before the guards change. The setup and physical release still need an operator check.
+
+The contributor's team published the reference implementation under MIT. The notice is in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. The public manuals explain the file roles, object calls and quality targets. The detailed JEScript call sequence, its arguments and the QN2 inputs follow the contributor's published implementation. Some of those interface details came from observed controller examples. Whether that reference meets this project's source rules is an open review question in #2945. The PR includes no vendor runtime, controller database, firmware or vendor program. The byte goldens are CamCraft output for original synthetic geometry.
+
+- [Agie-CAM source at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42)
+- [EZ-CAM AgieVision file workflow](https://www.ez-cam.de/downloads/v2017_edm_news.pdf)
+- [Kovoprog manual, section 3.4.1](https://www.kovoprog.cz/pictures/files/manuals/MainBook_kpd_en_open.pdf)
+- [Cimatron AgieVision quality targets](https://help.cimatron.com/en/2026/wizards/agievision/wedm_w_agv_step_5_7.htm)

+## #2946 - AGIECUT Classic 2S machine template
+
+Ship a machine library entry for setup. Section 1.1 (p. 4) gives the U and V limits relative to the vertical wire and the rapid speed for each axis. Section 5.2 (p. 44) lists electrode wires. The template includes the listed diameters within the standard Classic range of 0.20 to 0.33 mm. [AGIE technical data C2.1, June 2002](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf)
+
+Keep the X, Y and Z stroke lengths in the description. Centering them on zero would invent the endpoints in the user's setup. The taper rating depends on the guide and work height. Leave the taper limit and guide heights unset until the operator specifies the installation.
+
+The machine entry supplies no post or generator conditions. A wire operation needs a condition from the user's control before CamCraft can generate its path. An operator can save a configured copy of the template without changing the shipped file. Adding a native job writer requires separate control-specific sources and verification.

+## #2953 - Native Agie post for convex planar punches
+
+Keep the original single-solid proof and accept the complete nominal boundary of a convex vertical prism. The post uses its quantized five-decimal ISO polygon and checks convexity again before writing. The entry must lie on a supporting straight face. Measure the 3 mm separation transition along that face. Both clockwise and counterclockwise source polygons post counterclockwise with controller-owned compensation.
+
+Check the 20 mm QN2 rough offset of 0.245 mm and a 0.155 mm allowance for wire radius and clearance. A rounded join fits the original 0.4 mm stock margin. For a pointed join also check the intersection of the two outward-offset face lines. Since the stock is convex, connecting segments between the checked endpoints fit. A single clearance based on the polygon's bounding box misses long miters. A circular bound using the largest miter length would unnecessarily increase the 0.4 mm margin on axis-aligned rectangles.
+
+Preserve the refusal for reentrant profiles. A supported convex solid cannot contain an opposing wall in the exterior half-plane of an entry face. A concave punch needs a different full-prism proof and clearance checks between its nonadjacent faces. The controller file carries straight segments from the actual model boundary; fitting arcs to tessellated points can change the intended shape.
+
+Keep the drilled hole fixed when the exact perpendicular projection falls between ISO grid points. Use the closest exterior corner of its grid cell that is within 0.00001 mm of the projection (twice a coordinate half-unit). Check both exact and written separation room, the hole clearance of both written segments, convexity and the swept stock envelope. This can leave a microscopic amount of extra punch material. Unrestricted nearest rounding could remove material. Requiring exact collinearity would reject valid arbitrary slopes.

+# Post an Agie Classic Cut 2S job
+
+CamCraft writes the three native Agie files directly. The setup uses cold die steel (material 0001), Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and the resident QN2 Fine Ra 0.30 µm technology. Use this recipe only when those settings match the work and the installed control. The controller calculates the wire offsets and trim passes from that technology. CamCraft displays a wire-center preview with a representative finishing gap of 0.005 mm.
+
+## Post from the Wire EDM workspace
+
+1. Mount **AGIECUT Classic 2S (template)** as the setup machine. In the machine editor, open **EDM** and add a condition with ID **AGIE_QN2**, role **rough**, wire diameter **0.25 mm** and preview gap **0.005 mm**. Apply this change to the mounted machine. Choose **Agie native wire EDM** in the post picker.
+2. Define axis-aligned rectangular stock, 20 mm thick and at most 350 × 250 mm in plan. This span describes the stock. Verify the installed work datum and the available axis travel on Agie Control. CamCraft refuses profiles with a stated X or Y travel limit because its preview cannot check the full resident path against that limit. Put the first, unrotated work origin on the stock top. Its XY position determines the job coordinates.
+3. Use one modeled workpiece and create one **Wire Contour** on the complete punch model. Use a convex punch with straight sides, vertical walls and flat ends at the stock planes. Angled faces are supported. Leave at least 0.4 mm of stock around the nominal polygon. Acute corners can need more stock: the post also checks the intersection of the two offset face lines and the swept wire at that corner. On the tested 20 mm QN2 job, the rough wire centre ran 0.245 mm outside the punch. The stock margin includes the 0.125 mm wire radius. Additional bodies, selected subprofiles, holes, steps and concavities are refused. Select a 0.25 mm wire and condition **AGIE_QN2**. Set the work planes to the stock top and bottom, and specify how the punch is captured. The capture setting confirms support for the punch when it is released. Keep the wire vertical. Taper, four-axis, die cuts, burnout, explicit skims, tabs and fixture models are unsupported.
+4. Place the centre of a predrilled 2 mm threading hole in the waste. The entire hole must be inside the stock. Allow a perpendicular approach to the interior of a straight outside face with at least 3 mm of lead and at least 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Generate the operation.
+5. Open **Post**, choose **One program** and keep the general post settings at their defaults. Under **Agie technology**, set **Separation cut length (mm)** to **1.0**. Zero leaves the separation unspecified and blocks the post. This length applies to the separation segment that Agie Control generates. Check its position, trims and release sequence in the control’s job preview. Enter the parent folder and a fresh **Job folder name** such as `PUNCH40`. Use up to eight uppercase letters or digits, beginning with a letter. The post publishes the entire directory after validation. To retain an earlier job, give the new one a different name.
+
+## Try the synthetic punch
+
+From the project root, run the supplied script with a local CamCraft desktop CLI build.
+
+```sh
+cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
+```
+
+The script imports an original 40 × 20 × 20 mm rectangular punch, places it in 80 × 60 × 20 mm stock and sets the threading point at X−30 Y0. Its post call selects the native separation with `options: {separationLengthMm: 1.0}`. Stock top is Z0 in the Agie job. The `PUNCH40` directory contains the nominal contour in `PUNCH40.ISO`, its import reference in `PUNCH40.SBR` and the piece, start point and technology in `PUNCH40.SBL`. Existing destinations are refused. Edit the script’s output name to make another job.
+
+For an oblique entry, run `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` with a fresh `POLY20` destination. This pentagonal punch has a 3:4 sloping entry face. Its threading hole at X−20.5 Y6 approaches X−12.5 Y0 perpendicular to the middle of that face.
+
+Run `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/slope-punch.camscript` for a 7:10 entry face. The `SLOPE20` job keeps the drilled hole at X−20.5 Y6. Its perpendicular entry falls between five-decimal ISO coordinates. CamCraft can move the entry up to 0.00001 mm toward the waste while preserving the lead, separation room and rough-pass clearance.
+
+## Open the job in Agie Control
+
+Keep all three files together. In the control’s file manager, open **Imp/exp** and import the ISO object into **ISO Sys**. Then import the SBL into **SBL Sys**, keeping the matching SBR beside the SBL. In the workpiece list choose **New workpiece → Script Files**, select the imported SBL and confirm with **OK**.
+
+Open the new piece and check the configuration data against the intended setup. Run **FORMALCHECK** and inspect both errors and warnings. Save and close the piece, then run **GRAFICHECK** on that piece. Check the installed XY datum, available axis travel, entry from the drilled hole and compensation on the outside of the punch. In the tested 20 mm job, the main rough pass and three trims left a 1 mm section. The control then returned to cut and trim that section. Check the sequence and arrange support for release. CamCraft does not command a manual pause before the section cut.
